opening: Mumbai: The recent sell-off in Indian equities has pushed the Nifty Midcap 150 index into correction territory, with small-cap and micro-cap indices not far behind.
The Nifty Midcap 150 has fallen 10.2% from its 52-week high recorded on August 31, after declining 1.4% on Wednesday.
body: Although there is no universally accepted definition of a market correction, a decline of 10% or more, but less than 20%, from a recent high is generally considered one.

Many smaller stocks have broadly withstood the weak sentiment in the market and sharp declines in blue chips over the past two years thanks to a flood of retail money through equity mutual funds and directly.
But concerns over elevated valuations are beginning to catch up as investors evaluate whether the broader risk-off sentiment could impact future returns.
Over the past two years, the midcap and smallcap indices have each entered correction territory three times.
The smallcap index fell nearly 26% in this period, entering bear market territory but subsequently recovered.

This perception could be slowly shifting with valuations rising." What is perceived as a safe space can gradually become unsafe as valuations go up.
We are seeing corrections even in midcap and smallcap stocks, although this may not yet be visible at the index level," he said.

In the smallcap segment, 172 stocks have hit 52-week highs so far this year.
Of these, nine have declined 40-45% from their peaks, 32 have fallen 30-40%, 54 have lost 20-30%, and 77 are down 1-20%.

Of these, seven have fallen 40-50%, 23 have declined 30-40%, 64 have lost 20-30%, and 70 are down 1-20%.
Even after the recent declines, valuations are still at a premium over large-caps.
The mid-cap index is currently trading at a 42% premium to the Nifty, compared with its five-year average of 40%.

stories.title: Supreme Court Stays Investigation In Kerala FIR Against Ex-CM Pinarayi Vijayan & Kin In Exalogic Case For 10 Days
stories.summary: The Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and co-accused to file appeal before the High Court Division Bench against the Single Bench direction to register FIR.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court allowed Vijayan and co-accused to file appeal before the High Court Division Bench against the Single Bench direction to register FIR.

The Supreme Court today (October 21) held that former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter Veena T and son-in-law Muhammed Riyaz(a former Minister) are entitled to file appeal before the Division Bench of the Kerala High Court challenging the Single Bench's direction to register an FIR in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case on the basis of the information supplied to the Kerala.
Police by the Directorate of Enforcement.
Faulting the Division Bench's view that they do not have the locus to file the appeal, the Supreme Court set aside the Division Bench's order which refused leave to them to file an appeal.
The appeal was restored to the High Court's files.
To enable them to pursue the appeal before the Division Bench, the Supreme Court stayed the investigation in the FIR registered by the Kerala Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau for 7 days.

A special bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana observed that they can be held to be aggrieved parties in view of the Single Bench's view that there was material disclosing cognizable offence against them.
The petitioners were not made party in the writ petition filed before the Single Bench.

The Supreme Court expressed its inability to agree with the argument of the ED and the writ petitioner in the High Court that the petitioners had no right to be heard before the direction of registration of FIR.
"We are unable to agree...this is not a case where on receipt of communication under Section 66(2) PMLA, the State had registered FIR on its own.
On the contrary, the registration of FIR and commencement of investigation was pursuant to the order passed by the Constitutional Court.

While passing such order, the single bench had inter alia observed that the materials in the communication by the ED disclosed a cognizable offence and therefore it was obligatory for the State to register FIR.

stories.headline: LG Ladakh notifies amendment in record 6 days, council seats rationalised
stories.title: LG Ladakh notifies amendment in record 6 days, council seats rationalised
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 21: Ladakh is all set to hold elections to eight Autonomous Hill Development Councils after President Droupadi Murmu promulgated the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDC) (Amendment) Regulation, 2026. Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena notified the regulation with effect from October 19, terming it a “historic regulation”. Officials said the regulation was implemented in a record time of just six days. The Union Cabinet approved the amendments on October 14, followed by promulgation by the President on October 16. The regulation paves the way for creation of LAHDC in all eight districts of Ladakh, including the newly created Sankoo district. Ladakh earlier had only two hill councils — in Leh and Kargil, before the administration created five new districts including Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass in April and Sankoo on October 16. The amended regulation rationalises the number of constituencies from the earlier fixed 26 seats in each council to a minimum of seven seats and a maximum of 24 seats. It also provides for nomination of four members from ‘women’ and ‘unrepresented communities’ for greater people’s participation. Powers to conduct the polls have been assigned to the State Election Commission (SEC), which will be responsible for superintendence, direction and control of elections and preparation of electoral rolls. The regulation also substitutes the word ‘Governor’ with ‘Administrator’ throughout the LAHDC Act, 1997, defining Administrator as the Administrator of UT Ladakh appointed by the President under Article 239. “I am pleased to announce that upon the promulgation of the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (Amendment) Regulation, 2026, by the Hon’ble President of India, I have notified the regulation with effect from 19 October 2026. The historic regulation, implemented in a record time of just six days, now paves the way for creation of LAHDC in all 8 districts of Ladakh, including the newly created Sankoo district,” LG Ladakh posted on ‘X’. “The Union Cabinet had approved the amendments on 14 October, followed by its promulgation by the Hon’ble President on 16th October” LG Ladakh said. LG said that the amended regulation rationalises the number of constituencies – from the earlier 26 seats in each Council, to a minimum of 7 seats and maximum 24 seats now. It also provides for nomination of four members from “women” and “unrepresented communities” for greater people’s participation in the local governance. LG Saxena thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah for the “landmark regulation, that will strengthen grassroots democracy, enhance local representation and promote inclusivity”. However, leaders of the Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), which are spearheading agitation for constitutional safeguards and statehood, have opposed the amendment alleging that hill council powers have been curtailed and UT administration’s control strengthened. Under the new provisions, councils will exercise district-level Panchayat powers, while district plans will have to adhere to administrative guidelines and their bye-laws will require approval from the administration.

stories.headline: Ladakh makes judicial history
stories.title: Ladakh makes judicial history
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 21: A historic chapter in the Indian judicial history unfolded on Wednesday when Chief Justice of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh, Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Sanjay Parihar presided over the first regular division bench at Leh. The newly established Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh located at a breath-taking height of over 11,500 feet above sea level, began regular hearing of the cases from Wednesday. The day began with the hearing by the Division Bench in which the Chief Justice heard the matters through virtual mode while Justice Sanjay Parihar was present physically at the Ladakh Bench. After the conclusion of the hearing of five listed Division Bench matters, Justice Sanjay Parihar sat singly and dealt with as many as 60 matters listed before the single bench. Today’s proceedings made use of technology to facilitate a sort of hybrid hearing with the Chief Justice hearing through virtual mode and Justice Sanjay Parihar doing physical hearing. Justice Parihar said that the identification of the 65 cases that were listed today reflects the initial effort to organise and facilitate the hearing of matters concerning litigants from Ladakh. He said that the successful commencement of regular judicial hearings today by the Chief Justice in such a high-altitude location is a landmark achievement in the country’s judicial infrastructure and commitment to ensuring that geographical barriers do not become obstacles to justice. The establishment of the Ladakh Bench is a significant step in strengthening the reach of constitutional institutions to remote and geographically challenging regions of the country. Earlier, litigants from Leh, Kargil, and other far-flung areas of Ladakh would undertake lengthy journeys to Srinagar or Jammu for proceedings before the High Court. The commencement of hearings here is also encouraging for the legal fraternity of Ladakh including advocates. Ladakh Bench of J& K High court was formally inaugurated by the Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on October 18 at Melongthang, Leh.

stories.headline: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.title: PM Modi has failed ‘abysmally’ on Manipur, says Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge
stories.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi what has happened to the Peace Committee which was announced by home minister Amit Shah in June 2023 and what action has been taken on the Supreme Court-appointed Justice Gita Mittal Committee’s recommendations. He also asked what concrete measures have been taken to restore peace, protect citizens and address the continuing security challenges in the sensitive border state.

stories.headline: Div Com reviews alignment of Srinagar Ring Road Phase-III, Parimpora–Dalgate Flyover
stories.title: Div Com reviews alignment of Srinagar Ring Road Phase-III, Parimpora–Dalgate Flyover
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 21: Divisional Commissioner Kashmir, Anshul Garg on Wednesday chaired a meeting of officers to review the cahnge in proposed realignments of Srinagar Ring Road Phase-III (Lasjan–Pandach) and the Parimpora–Dalgate Flyover. The meeting was attended by the Commissioner, Srinagar Municipal Corporation (SMC); Deputy Commissioner Srinagar; SSP Traffic; Vice Chairman, Lakes Conservation and Management Authority (LCMA); Project Director, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI); and officers from the Roads and Buildings (R&B) Department, Irrigation and Flood Control Department, Srinagar Development Authority (SDA), and other concerned departments. During the review of Srinagar Ring Road Phase-III (Lasjan–Pandach), the Divisional Commissioner directed NHAI officials to compile comprehensive details of structures and departmental utilities falling within the proposed alignments including religious structures to access impediments & challenges and cost expenditure. He further directed the concerned authorities to explore modifications to the alignment to ensure that the road does not encroach upon the city's major water body. Reviewing the proposed alignment of the Parimpora–Dalgate Flyover, the Divisional Commissioner directed the R&B Department to explore an alternative alignments from Qamarwari to Nalamar and onward to Karanagar. He emphasized the need to ensure connectivity to key facilities, including SMHS Hospital, while minimizing traffic disruptions during the execution of the project. The concerned departments were directed to examine the proposed alignments in coordination with one another, keeping public convenience and essential infrastructure.
